        On Saturday, Saul "Canelo" Alvarez will enter the ring in the rare position of world title challenger. Alvarez will face WBC super middleweight champion Christian Mbilli in Saudi Arabia in Alvarez's first fight since September 2025.In Alvarez's previous fight, he suffered the most humbling defeat of his professional career, dropping a clear decision to Terence Crawford. Crawford was the much better fighter that night, using his world-class skills to beat Alvarez to the punch and constantly disrupt his rhythm.Unlike Alvarez's prior losses, he was not the far more inexperienced fighter facing a hall of famer (like against Floyd Mayweather Jr.) or the smaller man coming up in weight against a pound-for-pound elite (as was the case against Dmitry Bivol). Alvarez was younger than Crawford with a history of huge fights and Crawford was moving up multiple weight classes for the mega-payday of facing Canelo.Be sure to keep up with all the action on Saturday with our live coverage of Alvarez vs. Mbilli, including round-by-round scoring and updated fight results throughout the night!
What happened against Crawford seemed to validate all the doubts that had built up over the years. Alvarez has a ton of in-ring miles on his body at 36 and has seemed to have lost a few steps in recent years. Plus, Alvarez has not scored a stoppage since 2021. Time seemed to be catching up to Alvarez, and against a fighter as skilled as Crawford, there was no escape for the then-undisputed champion.
        
            
                Why the time is now for Canelo Alvarez to prove that he still has it on the elite, championship level
                
                    Brian Campbell                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
"After 20 years as a professional, I'm glad to be here," Alvarez said I'm the challenger now, but always in my mind, I'm the champion. Tune in on Saturday, because it's going to be a special night."I don't believe in shortcuts. I'm going straight for the champion because I already have the experience. I've been a champion for many years and I want to be a champion again."
Those doubts, and the question of how much Alvarez has left in the tank, lead us to Saturday and Mbilli, who was promoted from interim to full champion when Crawford retired following his win over Alvarez.Mbilli is a hard-charging fighter who has yet to taste defeat in his professional career, putting up a 29-0-1 pro record with 24 knockouts.Mbilli won the WBC interim belt with a first-round knockout of Maciej Sulecki, the second first-round knockout in a three-fight span for Mbilli. His first defense of the interim belt came against Lester Martínez on the undercard of Alvarez's fight with Crawford.
Against Martinez, Mbilli was on his usual game early, coming forward, throwing big right hands and working the body, but he fatigued down the stretch, which has been a recurring problem for the muscular Mbilli. The result of the fight was a very competitive draw that could have realistically gone either direction."My training camp was perfect. My mind is ready for this fight," Mbilli said. "I don't need to do anything special to win; I only need to be myself. That's how I'm going to win this fight." Let's take a closer look at the rest of the fight card on Saturday with the latest odds from DraftKings before getting to a prediction and expert pick on the main event below.
Mbilli vs. Alvarez fight card, oddsSaul "Canelo" Alvarez -330 vs. Christian Mbilli (c) +250, WBC super middleweight titleJaime Munguia -1800 vs. Nikita Zon +850, super middleweightsRafael Espinoza (c) -3000 vs. Ricardo Blandon +1100, WBO featherweight titleDavid Picasso -700 vs. Carl Jammes Martin +450, featherweightsReito Tsutsumi vs. Raymundo Rojas Garcia, junior lightweightsPredictionWere you to design a fighter in a lab who is most tailor-made for peak Alvarez, he'd look a lot like Mbilli. Mbilli doesn't have a deep bag of tricks, he comes forward and he throws big combinations with good body work. Mbilli doesn't have solid defense, and he has shown a tendency to fade as fights wear on. Add to those problems that Mbilli has only been scheduled for a 12-round fight once (his first-round knockout win over Sulecki), and you can see the areas that Alvarez has clear advantages.The biggest question for the fight is what Alvarez has left in the tank. He has spent more than two decades fighting at a professional level. There are no mountains really left to be conquered for Alvarez, and he has shown that, even if still great, he is well past his prime as a fighter.But has Alvarez faded enough that a simple pressure fighter -- even a good one -- able to break him down and collect a win?
It seems unlikely that Alvarez can't lean on his skills, defense and boxing IQ to roll through Mbilli on the scorecards. Mbilli leaves too many defensive openings and doesn't have the game to disrupt Alvarez the way Crawford did repeatedly. Alvarez should leave the ring as world champion once again.         The 2026-27 college basketball season begins Sunday when Villanova faces Notre Dame at Palazzo dello Sport in Rome, Italy. The season is starting a day earlier than usual after the NCAA granted special clearance for the teams to face each other in a monumental showdown. This matchup has been months in the making, with CBS Sports' Matt Norlander the first to report on it earlier this calendar year. The NCAA quietly approved a waiver in January to allow the teams a one-day head start, given the historic precedent of the matchup. Immediately following the men's game, Notre Dame's women's team will face Villanova. 
        
            
                Holy hoops! Villanova, Notre Dame finalizing plans to open 2026-27 college basketball season in Rome, Italy
                
                    Matt Norlander                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Notre Dame and Villanova are both prominent private Catholic schools with connections to Pope Leo XIV. Robert Francis Prevost is a 1977 alumnus of Villanova, and Notre Dame is regarded as the world's most prominent Catholic institution of higher learning. Notre Dame even has an outpost in Rome. While this matchup is historic on the men's side, it isn't unprecedented on the women's side. Duke opened last season against Baylor in Paris. This season, No. 1 South Carolina will face No. 20 Maryland on Nov. 2 at Adidas Arena in Paris. In 2023, South Carolina opened the season against Notre Dame at Halle Georges Carpentier Arena in Paris. 
With the season on the horizon, here is everything you need to know ahead of Villanova's matchup with Notre Dame on Sunday.  Villanova vs. Notre Dame: Need to know 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    A first for everything: The matchup between Villanova and Notre Dame is believed to be the first men's season opener on foreign soil and the first regular-season Division I basketball game in Italy. This matchup has been quite literally months in the making, with plans announced for this game nearly 10 months ago. This game will be played at Palazzetto dello Sport, which seats approximately 3,500 people for basketball and has been around since the 1950s. It remains unclear whether the Pope will attend the game: The Palazzetto dello Sport, the venue for the historic matchup, is located approximately 30 minutes from the Pope's residence in Vatican City. The Pope held a private audience on Saturday with all four teams and their traveling fans. Approximately 7,000 people are expected in the Paul VI audience hall inside the Vatican. 
New era for Notre Dame: The Fighting Irish were among the teams hit the hardest by the transfer portal earlier this offseason. Notre Dame's three leading scorers from last season (Markus Burton, Jalen Haralson and Cole Certa) all departed the program. With plenty of new faces and Notre Dame being on the verge of its longest NCAA Tournament drought since the 1990s, the pressure is on coach Micah Shrewsberry heading into Year 4 of his tenure. A win against a strong Villanova squad that won 24 games last season would be a great place to start. title: Thomas Castellanos' performance in win over Arizona raises ceiling for Texas Tech - CBS Sports
description: Joey McGuire's bold switch at quarterback unlocked a dormant rushing attack, giving the Red Raiders a dual-threat
body:
Joey McGuire's bold switch at quarterback unlocked a dormant rushing attack, giving the Red Raiders a dual-threat dimension that re-establishes them as Big 12 title contenders
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 31, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:38 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In the waning moments of No. 13 Texas Tech's game against No. 22 Arizona, the Red Raiders faced a critical opportunity to put the game away. First-time starting quarterback Thomas Castellanos took a carry for only a few yards on second down, pulling down the linebackers and setting up third-and-one. The Red Raiders lined up in a two-back set, seemingly setting up another quarterback run. Castellanos set the ball in the mesh point for a read while the defense collapsed. Instead of pulling, running back J'Koby Williams clutched the ball, took one cut right and broke off a dramatic 64-yard run to put the finishing touches on a dramatic 34-26 win to wrestle control of the Big 12 back. Texas Tech coach Joey McGuire made a bold move, benching quarterback Will Hammond in favor of the journeyman Castellanos. But after finding their offense in the second half, Castellanos unlocks a new ceiling for the Red Raiders heading into the home stretch. 
Castellanos was a late addition to the Texas Tech roster after receiving an injunction, primarily rostered to give the Red Raiders some experienced depth behind first-year starting quarterback Will Hammond. But several weeks into Hammond's starting tenure, results were poor. Despite playing a relatively light schedule, the Red Raiders ranked bottom half in the Big 12 in total offense under Hammond's watch. The running game, especially, was lackluster as defenses stacked the box and challenged an inconsistent offensive line. Hammond threw six touchdowns to six interceptions in his starts. While Castellanos is less of a factor in the passing game, the threat of his rushing is a game-changer for the Red Raiders. Seven of his carries went for first downs, and he broke off a pair of carries for 20-yard gains. Castellanos became the first Texas Tech quarterback to record 100 yards rushing since Tyler Shough. 
Castellanos threw for 144 yards and two touchdowns and added 117 yards and a score on the ground. But beyond the rushing production, defenses are forced to account for all 11 players. The switch made a huge difference for running back J'Koby Williams, who exploded for 175 yards and a touchdown in the win. The 328 yards rushing was the most surrendered by an Arizona defense since 2020, a 0-5 pandemic season under Kevin Sumlin. Since a 28-17 loss to BYU, the Wildcats have been on a tear. They won their last three games by an average of 28.0 points per game and rattled off a five-game winning streak. It was a prime opportunity for the Wildcats to knock off the reigning champs, coming off of a frustrating loss. Instead, Arizona gave up 34 points, the most since Sept. 27, 2025, against No. 14 Iowa State. 
To be clear, Castellanos has plenty of his own issues. The senior completed only 5 of 15 passes in the first half and 11 of 24 for the game, even below his career average of 58.5% completion. His passing is primarily a wrinkle on a run-based offense. Furthermore, Castellanos is still playing on a temporary injunction. Earlier this season, Castellanos briefly lost eligibility after a previous injunction was dissolved. Texas Tech can't be 100% confident that their new quarterback will stay eligible through the end of the season. Despite the drawbacks, Castellanos gives Texas Tech a much-needed spark heading into the home stretch of the season. With the 30-game starter in the lineup, the Red Raiders seriously re-enter the Big 12 race.

Plus, where to watch, what to know and a preview from an NFL expert

        One of the NFL's greatest rivalries is alive and well. On Sunday, the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns will duel with first place in the AFC North on the line. Both teams enter Sunday's game with 5-2 records. The Browns, by virtue of their Week 4 win over Pittsburgh, are technically the division leader. Cleveland responded to a loss to the Jets in Week 5 with wins over Baltimore and Tennessee. Pittsburgh has won three straight since losing to Cleveland. Last Sunday, the Steelers became the first team to win a game in Paris after recording a 16-10 win over the Saints. Here's how you can follow the action, along with a breakdown and a prediction. Where to watch Steelers vs. Browns liveWhen: Sunday, Nov. 1 | Time: 1 p.m. ETWhere: Acrisure Stadium -- Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania TV: CBS | Stream: Paramount+ Follow:  CBS Sports AppOdds: Steelers -3.5, O/U 39.5 (via DraftKings Sportsbook)Steelers vs. Browns: Need to know Last time we met: The Browns' 27-24 win over Pittsburgh in Week 4 was their fifth consecutive win over the Steelers in Cleveland. The Browns led 21-7 before withstanding Pittsburgh's comeback attempt. The Steelers' comeback was spearheaded by Aaron Rodgers, who threw two fourth-quarter touchdown passes. 
The Steelers tied the score with 1:42 left, but four completions by Deshaun Watson on Cleveland's ensuing drive set up Andre Szmyt's game-winning 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds remaining. Rodgers threw for 299 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions in a losing effort. Jaylen Warren ran for 93 yards on 17 carries, and DK Metcalf led Pittsburgh's receivers with 115 yards on five catches. Cleveland's offense ran through rookie receivers Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, who combined to catch nine passes for 153 yards. 
Steelers are finding their groove on both sides of the ball: Pittsburgh's three-game winning streak is largely the byproduct of better play from the offensive line and a defense that is continuously improving. Pittsburgh's offensive line surrendered five sacks of Rodgers back in Week 4. Rodgers has been sacked nine times in the three games since. While that's still not great, it is a sign of the unit's continuous improvement.The line has also helped revive the Steelers' rushing attack, which has improved further with Rico Dowdle's return. The duo specifically made their presence felt during Pittsburgh's game-winning drive in overtime in Tampa Bay back in Week 6. 
Defensively, the Steelers have made marked improvements since the loss in Cleveland, which was the Steelers' first game after Joey Porter Jr. was traded to Dallas. The unit is currently fifth in the NFL in points allowed, fourth in touchdown passes allowed, sixth in average yards per carry allowed, seventh in third-down efficiency and eighth in red zone efficiency. Linebacker Payton Wilson has been one of the Steelers' defensive standouts during the winning streak. He made a key interception during last week's win over the Saints. Browns offense ready to take off? While Cleveland's defense has been solid all year, its offense has at times left something to be desired. They are coming off their best performance in recent moments, however. 
Against the Titans, the Browns piled up 491 yards while receiving excellent balance. They threw for 308 yards and ran for 183. Cleveland did turn the ball over twice after not doing so a week earlier in a 13-10 win over the Ravens. Really, the big question in Cleveland is whether or not Watson can beat an elite defense. He'll try to show that he can on Sunday. Prediction The Steelers have two distinct advantages. They have the better quarterback and a running game that should be able to take advantage of a Browns defense that is 22nd in the NFL in average yards-per-carry allowed. If Dowdle and Warren get going, that should help open things up for Rodgers and the passing game. Score: Steelers 20, Browns 16

        There's arguably nothing scarier than settling down on Sunday morning, getting ready for the new slate to unfold, and having no clue what to wager on. This week in particular can leave some folks on their heels in the betting sphere. After all, when you're out all night trick-or-treating on Saturday night, who has the time to comb through all the latest news, injury updates, and anything else that could swing a game? Well, fortunately for you, you've come to the right place. We've fended off the urge to hunt for M&M's, Reese's, and other candy while dressed like our favorite comic-book hero and kept our eyes on the real prize: cashing our Week 8 bets. Below, you can find a pick for every matchup on the docket for Week 8, as well as five best bets. So, crack open some of your trick-or-treating haul from Halloween and let's bet! Note: New Orleans, New York (Giants), San Francisco, and Houston are on the bye in Week 8.Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville JaguarsSunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+)The Colts are already selling off parts amid a 2-5 start to the year, which includes a three-game losing skid entering Week 8. It's hard to see a scenario where things change for the better this weekend, as they'll head to Jacksonville to face a 4-2 Jaguars team that'll be fresh off its bye week. Coming into this slate, the Colts have a claim to be one of the worst offenses in the NFL. 
Their 4.5 yards-per-play average is tied for the worst in the league with the Eagles, and a large part of those issues lies at quarterback. Daniel Jones has yet to rekindle the version of himself from the first half of last year and has thrown an interception in all but one game so far in 2026. Jones ranks 31st out of 33 eligible quarterbacks in passer rating this season, while his EPA per dropback ranks 30th. Among quarterbacks with at least 100 pass attempts this year, Jones is tied for the second-highest turnover-worth-per-throw rate. He now faces a Jaguars pass defense that is just outside the top-10 in the league with an 87.7 passer rating allowed. They're also tied for the third-most interceptions (7) in the league. Conversely, you have Trevor Lawrence playing like an MVP candidate and should face little resistance from a Colts defense that has just two interceptions on the year. Projected score: Jaguars 33, Colts 20The pick: Jaguars -10Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati BengalsSunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+)The Bengals showed us their potential during their 35-point second-half outburst in the win over Baltimore. If anything close to that version of the Bengals is on the field on Sunday, Tennessee doesn't have a puncher's chance of keeping this close, especially after trading standout defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Bears earlier this week. The Titans' passing offense doesn't have the ceiling to go toe-to-toe with Joe Burrow, as the club ranks 29th in passer rating and is tied for last in yards per attempt.
While Cincinnati's offense garners much of the headlines, the Bengals' defense has been an underrated unit this season and was a key reason they were able to endure an offense-free first half in Week 7. Zac Taylor's defense has the third-best red zone efficiency (35% touchdown rate) in the NFL. That matches up well against a Tennessee red zone offense that scores a touchdown on just 47.4% of trips (27th in the NFL). Projected score: Bengals 35, Titans 21The pick: Bengals -12.5Los Angeles Chargers at Los Angeles RamsSunday, 4:05 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo, try for free)In theory, the Chargers would've spent the bye week figuring out what has gone wrong in their 0-6 start to the year and come out firing in Week 8, when they'll technically be the road team but will be at their home stadium as they face the Rams at SoFi Stadium. I just don't see them putting together much of a fight, however. Justin Herbert has been among the worst quarterbacks in the league so far this season and comes into Week 8 with a league-high 5.6% turnover-worthy throw rate. While the Rams haven't generated many turnovers, they have five interceptions this year, showing they are more than capable of taking advantage of any opportunity Herbert gives them. The Rams are also giving up just 186.3 passing yards per game this season, which is the fourth-lowest in the league. No matter which way you slice it, it should be tough sledding for Herbert in this matchup. 
That means Matthew Stafford likely won't have to do much heavy lifting to clear this 6.5-point spread. That's especially true considering that the Chargers can be taken advantage of on the ground. They're allowing 123.8 rushing yards per game, so this could be a matchup where Kyren Williams and Blake Corum become the focal point of the attack. That backfield duo is coming off a win against the Raiders where they each went for over 90 yards rushing to go along with a touchdown. It wouldn't be shocking to see similar production on Sunday. Projected score: Rams 30, Chargers 17The pick: Rams -6.5New England Patriots at Miami DolphinsSunday, 4:25 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+)The Dolphins finally got into the win column for the first time all season with a road win against the Jets. While that's great for Jeff Hafley's club to get off the schneid, I don't see the momentum from that victory turning into a two-game winning streak. Since Mike Vrabel became the head coach, New England is 8-4-1 ATS on the road. As a road favorite in games, they are 3-2 ATS with an average margin of victory of 13 points. While they'll be on the road, the Patriots have the rest advantage in this game after playing last Thursday. They're also simply the better team. Miami is allowing 5.7 yards per play this season and 7.8 yards per pass attempt (tied for third-highest in the NFL). Drake Maye should continue to find success through the air against a Dolphins secondary that is allowing a league-high 116.8 passer rating against. So long as they don't shoot themselves in the foot, this should be a double-digit victory for New England. 
Projected score: Patriots 30, Dolphins 20The pick: Patriots -7Philadelphia Eagles at Washington CommandersSunday, 8:20 p.m. (NBC, Stream: Fubo, try for free)The Philadelphia Eagles have been ravaged by injuries, and they aren't getting any reprieve on the schedule either. After playing on Monday night, the Eagles will head on the road for a short week to face a Commanders team coming off its bye week. That's as lopsided a rest advantage as you'll find in the NFL this season. The Commanders did lose No. 1 wideout Terry McLaurin for the season due to a torn patellar tendon he suffered in Week 6. While the offense does take a hit in his absence, there are guys who can step up. Along with Stefon Diggs, rookie wideout Antonio Williams has flashed potential, while veteran tight end Chig Okonkwo has been an underutilized piece of the offense that I expect will see more work down the stretch. Washington's defense won't be mistaken for one of the best units in the league, but I think they should be able to keep Tanner McKee in check. That's especially true after watching Saquon Barkley on Monday night, as the Eagles running back was clearly limited with a hamstring injury. If he suits up on Sunday, it's hard to imagine he'll be any healthier, capping the ceiling of the Eagles offense. Philadelphia is also 0-2 ATS on the road so far this season with a -8.0 average margin of victory.

        No. 3 Georgia and No. 17 Florida will be squaring off somewhere other than Jacksonville for the first time since 1995 on Saturday, as the historic rivals take the World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party indoors at Atlanta's Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Saturday. With Jacksonville's EverBank Stadium under renovation until August 2028, the setting will be different.The stakes remain the same. In fact, there may be an even higher degree of intensity to this year's showdown between the border foes because of the circumstances. It's the first time since 2020 that both are ranked in the top 20 of the AP poll. Georgia (6-1, 4-1 SEC) is coming off a bye week after a stunning home loss to Auburn, and Florida (5-2, 3-2) is riding high off an Oct. 17 road win over Texas. First-year Gators coach Jon Sumrall already has two wins over top-10 teams (Ole Miss and Texas) and could get his team firmly in the College Football Playoff hunt with another marquee win.The Bulldogs have won five straight meetings in the series, but Sumrall has reinvigorated the Florida program this season since arriving from Tulane. The Gators have shown the ability to slay some of the SEC's top dogs already this season, and Georgia will need to be on high alert to avoid suffering consecutive regular season losses for the first time since Kirby Smart's first season in 2015.
Where to watch Georgia vs. Florida liveDate: Saturday, Oct. 31 | Time: 3:30 p.m. ETLocation: Mercedes-Benz Stadium -- Atlanta, GeorgiaTV: ESPN | Live stream: Fubo (try free)  Georgia vs. Florida: Need to know  Florida's quarterback situation: Starting in place of the injured Aaron Philo, Florida sophomore Tramell Jones Jr. rose to the occasion in a Week 7 win at Texas. The inexperienced quarterback completed 22 of 35 passes for 155 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions against the Longhorns' vaunted defense while also totaling 41 rushing yards. But will he play against Georgia? Philo was listed as questionable on the Gators' first student-athlete availability report this week, raising questions over who will get the nod under center. Florida coach Jon Sumrall said Monday that he doesn't plan to name a starter before the game, which will force Georgia to prepare for both QBs. Jones is more mobile, but he's also put his full repertoire on tape now. Philo is still dealing with a right shoulder injury, but he did practice this week.Georgia's run defense: Regardless of who starts at quarterback for Florida, the Gators are going to try and lean on their run game. Georgia's run defense has shown some vulnerability in the past two games. Led by quarterback Byrum Brown, Auburn totaled 192 yards rushing against the Bulldogs in an Oct. 17 upset road win over UGA. The week before, Alabama amassed 161 yards on the ground against Georgia. Up until those two games, Georgia's run defense had been stout. Facing Florida might be the toughest test yet of Georgia's ability to stop the run. The Gators raced to a 4-0 start, including wins over Auburn and Ole Miss, by rushing for 200+ yards in each game. The UF rushing game has been less effective in three games since then, but star back Jadan Baugh is a load to handle. He leads the SEC in rushing touchdowns with 13 and is third in rushing yards with 763.
CFP implications: Georgia's chances of reaching the College Football Playoff will rise to 94.5% with a win, according to the CBS Sports CFP Forecaster. Those odds would dip to 72.7% with a loss. Entering Saturday, Florida has just a 9.5% chance to make it, but that mark would surge to 29% with an upset win over the Bulldogs. On the flip side, suffering a third loss would leave UF with just a 5.6% chance of making the playoff. If the Gators suffer a third loss against Georgia, they would need to run the table against Oklahoma, Kentucky, Vanderbilt and Florida State and then get some help from other teams to have any shot at reaching the field with a 9-3 record.Georgia vs. Florida prediction, picksExpect to see an angry Georgia team after the Bulldogs were forced to stew on a turnover-fueled home loss to Auburn during a bye week. Florida will have the Bulldogs' full attention after an upset win at Texas, and UGA won't be remotely caught off guard by anything the Gators attempt offensively. Georgia's defensive staff knows Florida offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner well. On the opposite side, the Gators have shown they are vulnerable on defense, and Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton will be playing with a chip on his shoulder after a rare poor performance against Auburn. Pick: Georgia -12.5

Renato Moicano and Tom Nolan join the fray at UFC Fight Night on Saturday, taking place at the Meta APEX in Las Vegas.Moicano (21-7-1) demanded money fights after dispatching hungry prospect Chris Duncan in April. Brian Ortega offered exactly what Moicano wanted; however, two "T-City" withdrawals left "Money" Moicano empty-handed. Uninterested in booking Ortega a third time, Moicano made the financially wise but competitively risky choice to headline opposite another eager contender."They offered the Nolan fight on the same card [UFC 332], and I said, Let's do a main event.' I have respect for Tom Nolan, and I think he needs time to have a camp," Moicano told CBS Sports. "It's one thing to beat him on one week's notice. I gave him that chance to be better prepared for this fight."Sign up for Paramount+ and watch UFC for no additional fee -- every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night is included with your subscription! "It's one thing beating Brian Ortega coming out of three losses or four losses," he said earlier in the interview. "Another thing is beating a 26-year-old guy coming off five wins, knockouts, and all that stuff. Very good. So, I think that shows that I'm still in the game."
Nolan (11-1) has not lost sight of the opportunity ahead of him. Quillan Salkilld, Paddy Pimblett and Salahdine Parnasse are among the young stars replacing the longstanding lightweight elite. Nolan can be part of a changing tide in the division by knocking off Moicano, whom he grew up watching. He's also uniquely equipped, having studied Moicano's win over Benoit Saint Denis as he prepared for his breakout fight against Fares Ziam."The way he used the body triangle to go between mount and back mount. I just thought it was a beautiful way to keep his hips facing the floor at all times," Nolan told CBS Sports. "There are only a few examples of it at a really high level to study, and you know, I'm a big believer in keeping up with the times and studying the sport."
There's no better way to honor a fighting legend than to take them out. If Nolan has it his way, he'll utilize some of Moicano's signature moves against him."Ground and pound. Some elbows would be very nice. Just slicing and dicing would be sick," Nolan said. "He's very good at that. I'd love to do that to him."The co-main event resembles the marquee fight. Jacobe Smith is foaming at the mouth for a ranking. Beating an experienced veteran like Randy Brown, 36, would do wonders for the 30-year-old's campaign. Smith boasts a serious wrestling pedigree as an NCAA Division I All-American representing Oklahoma State, but he's a born fighter. Smith has a mean streak, evident in his interviews and his seven straight stoppages. Taking out Brown will be his warning shot to the division.
"I'm very well equipped to get you out of there, whether it's wrestling, choking you out, or knocking you out," Smith told CBS Sports. That's the dilemma on Saturday. Moicano looked refreshed after knocking out Chris Duncan in April, but now faces a scrappy, dynamic prospect 11 years his junior. Nolan has the tools to knock out Moicano, whose chin isn't the sturdiest. But Nolan's offense-first approach also leaves him vulnerable to mistakes against a savvy, seasoned opponent like Moicano. Expect a relatively short fight with momentum swings. Nolan is especially dangerous in the first 10 minutes, and a knockout shouldn't surprise anyone. But I'm not sold on his resume yet. His upset win over Ziam was impressive, though Ziam's subsequent loss takes some shine off the result. Moicano's recent resurgence inspired enough confidence to exploit openings. title: Fantasy Football Week 8 start 'em, sit 'em: Geno Smith poised for big game, Patrick Mahomes faces tough matchup - CBS Sports

body:
Week 8 brings another wave of difficult decisions for Fantasy managers, with four teams on bye, injuries continuing to reshape starting lineups and several familiar names facing challenging matchups. With the Fantasy regular season approaching its midpoint, finding the right balance between trusting proven performers and taking advantage of favorable matchups could make all the difference.Geno Smith is among the quarterbacks worth trusting this week, with a favorable matchup against his former team, the Raiders, creating an opportunity for another strong performance. Michael Wilson could also bounce back against a vulnerable Cowboys secondary, while Sam LaPorta remains a reliable option despite an inconsistent season. Meanwhile, KC Concepcion's recent breakout has put him firmly in the flex conversation as Cleveland prepares for a rematch with Pittsburgh.On the other side, Patrick Mahomes faces another difficult matchup against Denver, while Jared Goff could struggle against Minnesota's relentless blitz-heavy defense. Quinshon Judkins also faces a tougher challenge against Pittsburgh's stout run defense, and Caleb Williams must contend with a Seattle defense that has consistently frustrated opposing quarterbacks. Even productive Fantasy starters can become risky plays when defensive schemes and offensive tendencies work against them.That's where Dave Richard's Week 8 matchup breakdown comes in. From defensive coverages and pass-rush pressure to backfield workloads and target distribution, we'll examine the factors that matter most to help you identify trustworthy starters, avoid potential disappointments and make the best possible lineup decisions.

One of Bryce Young's biggest strengths turned into an exploitable weakness in a hurry last week when the Buccaneers swarmed his offensive line, resulting in a 15.6% sack rate when Young was in the game. The crazy part? The Bucs had a season-low blitz rate (28.9%) and a season-high non-blitz pressure rate (44%). Young's O-line also took some hits with right tackle Taylor Moton fracturing his fibula and left guard Damien Lewis not well enough to play on Thursday. Young is a considerably worse quarterback when pressured, throwing a catchable ball at a 58% rate at 5.9 yards per attempt. There's no doubt the Packers aren't as aggressive as the Bucs were, but they will try to copy a lot of what the Buccaneers did versus a depleted offensive line. Having confidence in Young bouncing back is a little tough, particularly since only one QB has had north of 18 Fantasy points against Green Bay since Week 2 (Jared Goff had 22 Fantasy points last week).  It also doesn't help that the Packers lead the NFL with eight interceptions (they dropped two more last week) and rank in the top 10 in yards allowed per attempt to receivers despite seeing the third-most WR targets. They also own the third-best EPA per dropback against slot receivers and the best yards per attempt allowed to slot receivers. That's a warning salvo against Jalen Coker, who lines up in the slot about half the time. MUST-START: Chuba Hubbard, Christian Watson, Matthew Golden, Tetairoa McMillanSTART: Jordan Love, Bryce Young (borderline start), Josh Jacobs, Jalen Coker, Tucker KraftSIT: Darren Waller, Tommy Tremble, Packers DST, Panthers DST

That's been relatively consistent with Jesse Minter's defense, though their Cover-4 shell has at times operated as man-to-man. And the Ravens pass rush has been decent, but it has really come through against weaker offensive lines, which the Bills don't have. That ties into the Bills run game, which should have success against the Ravens, much like other strong run games, like Indy, Dallas and Atlanta have had against them this season. When Cook gets fed, Buffalo's pass-catchers starve -- only once in four of Cook's games with 20-plus carries has a Bills wideout notched over 14 PPR points (Keon Coleman, Week 6, 15 PPR), and only twice have any Bills pass-catcher gone over that number (Dalton Kincaid had 22.5 against Detroit). The Ravens pass defense isn't one to fear, but this is about the Bills' offensive tendencies when they're able to run the ball. It keeps D.J. Moore, Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir from being appealing Fantasy options, even in what's supposed to be a high-scoring game. Moore is obviously decent, the others aren't particularly great. A final point: Of the four touchdowns allowed to wideouts by the Ravens this season, just one (Ja'Marr Chase's two-yard TD last week) came from a receiver lined up wide.

Pollard's been slightly more efficient running in the zone scheme compared to the gap scheme, and that's specifically the run game the Bengals have shown improvement against. The Bengals have also tackled better on runs in their past two games. But things just might work out this week for Wilson versus a Dallas defense that has played a little more man-to-man coverage on third downs, particularly when they blitz the quarterback. The Cowboys have also played the seventh-most single-high safety coverage in the league. Both of these factors really help Wilson, who has a Cardinals-best 36% target per route run rate and 2.11 yards per route rate average against single-high this season (and both numbers have boosted to 41.7% and 2.33 in two games since the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade). Wilson also attracts plenty of targets against man-to-man (32.8% target rate, but just 1.6 yards per route run). Jared Goff's track record against Brian Flores' Vikings has actually been pretty good -- between 22 and 24.8 Fantasy points in three of his past five games -- but last Christmas was his absolute worst outing against him when he scored 4.1. Goff was blitzed a ton and forced to keep his passes relatively short (a common theme in his matchups with the Vikings). The only difference between last year's Vikings and this year's Vikings is that this year's Vikings are even more aggressive and are willing to blitz wayyy more than they have in the past. Their lowest blitz rate in a game this season was 56.5%, and their highest was last week against the Colts when they blitzed on 85.2% of Daniel Jones' dropbacks. The Lions rank seventh-best in pass rush pressure rate allowed, and tops in the NFL in pass rush pressure rate allowed when blitzed, but they're among the least-blitzed offenses in the NFL for good reason. The Vikings won't care; they're going to blitz Goff mercilessly and thus be a huge test for Detroit's O-line, and that's enough reason to be wary of anything more than a solid game from him.
You could have probably guessed that when Goff has been pressured and/or blitzed this season, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs have been his top-targeted teammates. But Sam LaPorta is third, landing a target per route run rate close to St. Brown's when Goff's pressured, and close to the same yard per route run rate as St. Brown when Goff is blitzed (2.77 yards for LaPorta is awfully good). LaPorta's lack of targets last week was a little bit about him chipping defenders on his way out on his route and more about Goff having time to attack downfield. But Liam Coen spoke this week about creating more explosive runs, particularly when his offensive line carries out its assignment. In their past three games, it's been Chris Rodriguez with a better rushing average (5.0) and better explosive run rate (10.8%) than Tuten (3.6 and 9.8%). It's kind of hard to buy into Rodriguez displacing Tuten, but the case can be made for both to split duties to some degree. Blended with the Raiders' single-high safety coverages when they play man or zone (usually zone), this should be a second-straight good game for Geno Smith. Not only might he need to throw a good amount, but his passing is more explosive against one-high looks than two-high. It would make sense for Smith to work on connecting with Garrett Wilson more -- Wilson's got some great numbers this season against Cover-1, which the Raiders will play their man-to-man coverage in. But Omar Cooper Jr. has been a winner for the Jets both on short routes and deep ones, and he's been great against single-high coverage in limited action. Maybe there's a teeny concern about the Jets run game succeeding to the point where Smith won't have to throw a ton. Still, the Raiders have defended a quarterback that's dropped back at least 30 times in every game this season, and if they're not going to pressure like they did earlier, then Smith should have time to rip some shots downfield against his old squad.

And last week, Braelon Allen became the sixth consecutive running back to notch at least 15.8 PPR points on the Dolphins. This isn't to tell you the obvious advice to start Rhamondre Stevenson, who has a hammerlock on the Patriots' high-value RB touches, but it is to tell you that unless the Dolphins offense can put up some points, we might not see a ton of passing from Drake Maye. Henry, along with rookie tight end Eli Raridon, has been among Maye's trusted red-zone targets since Week 4. And in the two games before A.J. Brown returned we saw Efton Chism III develop chemistry with Maye, coming up with modest 12.2 and 10.9 PPR point games on a five-target-per-game average. Mind you, those were in games he split reps with Romeo Doubs and, for one game, Mack Hollins. Like Brown, those guys aren't available this week, creating a pathway for Chism to be busy against an exploitable Dolphins secondary. He had target per route rates over 20% and yard per route rates over 2.0 in Weeks 4 and 5. He's my favorite Patriots receiver with Brown sidelined, but not quite a top-36 choice.

The specific zone coverages they subscribe to are Caleb Williams' worst in terms of EPA per dropback, and Cover-6 has netted Williams a weak 3.2-yard average depth of throw this season. It's fair to expect this defense to give Williams problems, but in his limited snaps this season, Williams has definitely leaned on Luther Burden III against both Cover-3 (26.5% target per route run, 2.62 yards per route run) and Cover-6 (37.5% target per route run rate, 3.5 yards per route run). These are exceptional numbers that keep Burden in the starting conversation. Colston Loveland should be right there with him -- he's seen a 27.3% target per route rate with Williams in his past two games for just over two yards per route, and his 18.2% target per route rate against Cover-6 is second-best among Bears regulars, albeit with a weak 0.27 yards per route run. All of the other Bears players, including D'Andre Swift, carry some risk. Receptions have helped five running backs get at least 13 PPR points against the Seahawks, but only Christian McCaffrey has had over 15 PPR points this season. Lips were sealed among Seahawks coaches this week -- they were asked about Quenton Nelson's addition more than anything else (though we did learn the Seahawks do plan to keep leaning into the quick-passing game). Buss accused her siblings of a 'cloak and dagger' campaign through the media in a court filing this week

        Jeanie Buss has accused her siblings of conspiring against her in a "cloak and dagger" campaign through the media in a court filing this week and has asked a judge to block her siblings' attempts to sell the family's shares of the Los Angeles Lakers, ESPN reports.According to Wednesday's filing, Jeanie Buss said her siblings -- specifically Joey and Jesse Buss -- are jealous of their father's decision to leave her with governor rights to the team and she does not want them selling the family's remaining shares of the team.Finality for both sides of the legal spat could come during a scheduled Dec. 8 hearing in Los Angeles Superior Court.Former Disney CEO Bob Iger and Josh Kushner spearhead an ownership group looking to buy the Lakers from Mark Walter at a valuation of $12.5 billion. 

        
            
                Jeanie Buss disputes her family's sale of Lakers stake: What to know about dramatic off-court fight
                
                    Sam Quinn                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
"The conflicts that ensued after Dr. (Jerry) Buss's death (in 2013) were sadly inevitable, and no doubt intensified given that Dr. Buss chose his daughter over four sons to be his successor," representation for Jeanie Buss wrote in this week's filing. "Respondents' obsession with tearing down Jeanie and their inability to accept that she would be a part of the Lakers' future is borne of this classic succession parable."Jeanie Buss would no longer serve as the Lakers' governor if her family sells its 17.8% ownership stake, which is just above the NBA's 15% minimum for the family to retain control. Iger previously said during an interview with The California Post that the plan was for Buss to remain governor, but "if things change, they'll change." The latest filing continues an ongoing saga between family members over the NBA's third-most valuable franchise. Earlier this year, ESPN reported that Jeanie Buss contended that a 2017 court order prevents any vote to sell the remaining family shares without her consent. 
That was not the first time that the Buss siblings have fought over control of the team. When Jeanie fired Jim Buss as head of basketball operations in 2017, he and Johnny Buss attempted to strip Jeanie of her seat on the Lakers' board of directors. The two sides ultimately agreed to settle with Jeanie Buss remaining in control of the team.Now, Jeanie Buss is asking the court to remove two siblings as co-trustees of the trust for breach of fiduciary duty, hold them in contempt of court, and "find Jim, Johnny and Jesse liable for aiding and abetting a violation of the 2017 court order and be reimbursed for legal costs," per ESPN.
If the Buss family sells the entirety of its shares of the team, each sibling receives an additional $371 million per go-along rights. ESPN reported this week that settlement talks have begun."Jeanie had no choice but to seek court intervention to enforce the clear terms of the trust and this court's 2017 order," Wednesday's filing states. "Respondents respond (by) casting themselves as victims, when in reality, the entire episode is their own false flag operation."The cloak and dagger, backroom 'votes' and 'resolutions' shared with ESPN, rather than their co-trustee and sister, and subsequent refusal to discuss the matter, was intended to force Jeanie's hand, cry victim and again smear her in the media by sharing in advance their specious response."

Chiefs vs. Broncos need to knowDivision: This division is a close one, especially with K.C.'s loss last week.
